newsitem.title: USA: Weyerhaeuser to close recycling plants, sees charge.
newsitem.headline: Weyerhaeuser to close recycling plants, sees charge.

text.p: Weyerhaeuser Co. said Monday it will close some of its recycling plants and sell a nursery business in Connecticut to sharpen its focus on its core paper and forest products business.
The paper and pulp maker said it would take an after-tax charge of about $25 million, or 12 cents a share, in the first quarter for one-time costs related to the moves.
Weyerhaeuser, which is based in Tacoma, Wash, said it would close or dispose of recycling facilities and related assets in Longview, Wash.
It also said it plans to sell Shemin Nurseries, a wholesale nursery business based in Danbury, Conn.

"Recycling remains a core business, but we must make some adjustments to our nationwide system to meet the needs of customers in an increasingly competitive marketplace," said President John Creighton Jr.
Weyerhaeuser stock rose 25 cents to $46.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
